[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/ardata-fr/munch/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ardata-fr/munch/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)

> 'munch' crunches markdown text and 'flextable' paragraphs into grid graphics.

'munch' started as internal code in 'flextable' for rendering rich text with
'grid'. It was extracted into its own package to also serve 'ggiraph' and to 
provide unified formatting between 'ggplot2' graphics and 'flextable' tables.

'munch' lets you produce this annotated graphic:

```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.height=6, fig.width=7}
library(ggplot2)
library(officer)
library(flextable)
library(munch)
library(gdtools)

fset <- font_set_liberation()
set_flextable_defaults(
  font.family = "Liberation Sans",
  font.size = 19
)
r_logo <- file.path(R.home("doc"), "html", "logo.jpg")
set_theme(theme_minimal(base_family = "Liberation Sans", base_size = 11))
dat <- subset(diamonds, cut %in% c("Premium", "Ideal"))

# Title: image + bold + italic
title_chunks <- as_paragraph(
  as_image(src = r_logo, width = 0.25, height = 0.2),
  as_chunk(" "),
  as_b("Diamond"),
  as_chunk(" pricing - "),
  as_i("Premium"),
  as_chunk(" vs "),
  as_i("Ideal")
)
set_flextable_defaults(
  font.size = 11
)
# Subtitle: colorize + highlight
subtitle_chunks <- as_paragraph(
  colorize("Premium", color = "#C36A1C"),
  as_chunk(" (n = "),
  as_highlight(as.character(sum(dat$cut == "Premium")), color = "#FDDBC7"),
  as_chunk(") and "),
  colorize("Ideal", color = "#1F78B4"),
  as_chunk(" (n = "),
  as_highlight(as.character(sum(dat$cut == "Ideal")), color = "#D1E5F0"),
  as_chunk(")")
)
set_flextable_defaults(
  font.size = 9
)
# Caption: superscript + subscript + strikethrough
caption_chunks <- as_paragraph(
  as_chunk("R"),
  as_sup("2"),
  as_chunk(" = 0.85 · "),
  as_i("no effect"),
  as_chunk(" · "),
  colorize("H", "#E31A1C"),
  colorize(as_sub("0"), "#E31A1C"),
  colorize(as_chunk(" rejected"), "#E31A1C"),
  "\n",
  as_i("Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, ut platea nullam odio dui in. Placerat gravida. Pretium phasellus non, dolor suscipit at aliquet, mollis venenatis per. Mus leo ante ligula. Mattis neque etiam sagittis risus facilisis vel ut, non quis eu. Iaculis, mauris porta orci et natoque nisl habitant ac eget.")
)

set_flextable_defaults(
  font.size = 10
)
# Axis labels: bold + color via fp_text_lite
ylab_chunks <- as_paragraph(
  as_chunk("Price", props = fp_text_lite(bold = TRUE, color = "#2C3E50")),
  as_chunk(" (USD)")
)
xlab_chunks <- as_paragraph(
  as_chunk("Carat", props = fp_text_lite(bold = TRUE, color = "#2C3E50")),
  as_chunk(" weight")
)

ggplot(dat, aes(carat, price, color = cut)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .1, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Premium = "#C36A1C", Ideal = "#1F78B4")) +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#EFEFEF", colour = "transparent"),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#EFEFEF", colour = "transparent"),
    plot.title = element_chunks(title_chunks, hjust = .5),
    plot.subtitle = element_chunks(subtitle_chunks, hjust = .5),
    plot.caption = element_chunks(caption_chunks, lineheight = 1.5, hjust = 0),
    plot.caption.position = "plot",
    axis.title.x = element_chunks(xlab_chunks, hjust = 1),
    axis.title.y = element_chunks(ylab_chunks, hjust = 1)
  )
```

The title, subtitle, caption and axis labels above are all built with
`element_chunks()` and 'flextable' paragraph objects, bold, italic,
colors, highlights, superscripts, subscripts, strikethrough and an
embedded image.

| Function | Purpose | Input |
|----------|---------|-------|
| `element_md()` | Markdown in theme elements | Character string |
| `element_chunks()` | Advanced formatting in theme elements | `as_paragraph()` object |
| `geom_text_md()` | Markdown text annotations | `label` aesthetic |
| `geom_label_md()` | Markdown labels with background | `label` aesthetic |

## Installation

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("ardata-fr/munch")
```

## Supported graphics devices

'munch' requires graphics devices that support 'systemfonts':
['ragg'](https://ragg.r-lib.org/), ['svglite'](https://svglite.r-lib.org/), or
['ggiraph'](https://davidgohel.github.io/ggiraph/).
'cairo' devices is also supported when fonts are installed at the system level.
See `vignette("font-recipes")` for font configuration, alternative devices,
and troubleshooting.

## Quick start

### ggplot2

Use `element_md()` for markdown in theme elements, and `geom_text_md()` or
`geom_label_md()` for annotations:

```{r ggplot-example, fig.height=3.5, message=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt)) +
 geom_point() +
 labs(title = "**Fuel consumption** vs *Weight*") +
 theme(plot.title = element_md(size = 16))
```

For advanced formatting (superscripts, subscripts, colors), use `element_chunks()`
with 'flextable' paragraph objects:

```{r element-chunks-example, fig.height=3.5, message=FALSE}
title_chunks <- as_paragraph(
 as_chunk("Model: R"), as_sup("2"), as_chunk(" = 0.75")
)

ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt)) +
 geom_point() +
 theme(plot.title = element_chunks(title_chunks))
```

#### Syntax comparison

| Syntax | `element_md()` | `element_chunks()` |
|--------|----------------|-------------------|
| Bold / Italic | `**text**` / `*text*` | `as_b()` / `as_i()` |
| Inline code | `` `code` `` | x |
| Strikethrough | `~~text~~` | `as_strike()` |
| Superscript | x | `as_sup()` |
| Subscript | x | `as_sub()` |
| Custom colors | x | `colorize()` |
| Highlighting | x | `as_highlight()` |

### Patchwork integration

Use `munch_annotation()` as a drop in replacement for `patchwork::plot_annotation()` 
which accepts `element_chunk()` and `element_md()` to add rich-text titles, subtitles, 
and captions — including auto-wrapping — to combined plots:

```{r patchwork-example, fig.height=4, fig.width=7, message=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

p1 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = "MPG", y = "Weight")

p2 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(hp, wt)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Horsepower", y = "Weight")

title_chunks <- as_paragraph(
  as_b("Motor Trend"), as_chunk(" — engine performance, 1974")
)

caption_chunks <- as_paragraph(
  as_chunk("R"), as_sup("2"), as_chunk(" = 0.75 · "),
  as_i("Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, ut platea nullam odio dui in. "),
  as_i("Placerat gravida. Pretium phasellus non, dolor suscipit at aliquet, "),
  as_i("mollis venenatis per. Mus leo ante ligula.")
)

wrap_plots(p1, p2) +
  munch_annotation(
    title   = element_chunks(title_chunks),
    caption = element_chunks(caption_chunks, lineheight = 1.5, hjust = 0)
  )
```

For plain markdown text, pass the content as a string and use `element_md()`
in the `theme` argument — the same pattern as regular ggplot2 theming:

```{r patchwork-example-md, fig.height=4, fig.width=7, message=FALSE}
wrap_plots(p1, p2) +
  munch_annotation(
    title   = "**Motor Trend** — engine performance, 1974",
    caption = "R^2^ = 0.75 · *Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, ut platea nullam odio dui in. Placerat gravida pretium phasellus non, dolor suscipit at aliquet.*",
    theme   = theme(
      plot.title   = element_md(),
      plot.caption = element_md(lineheight = 1.5, hjust = 0)
    )
  )
```

The caption auto-wraps to the full figure width at render time, so it works
correctly regardless of output size. `title`, `subtitle`, and `caption` each
accept an `element_chunks()` or `element_md()` object, a bare `as_paragraph()`
object, or a plain character string.

### flextable

Use `as_paragraph_md()` for markdown in table cells:

```{r flextable-example, message=FALSE}
ft <- flextable(head(iris, 3))
ft <- mk_par(ft, j = 1, part = "header",
 value = as_paragraph_md("*Sepal* **Length**"))
autofit(ft)
```

### Markdown to grob

```{r md-grob-basic}
library(munch)
library(grid)

gr <- md_grob("This is **bold** and *italic* text.")
grid.newpage()
grid.draw(gr)
```

For superscripts, subscripts, or colors not available in markdown, use 'flextable'
chunks with `chunks_grob()`:

```{r chunks-formula, fig.width=2, out.width="200px"}
library(flextable)

chunks <- as_paragraph(as_chunk("E = mc"), as_sup("2"))
gr <- chunks_grob(chunks)
grid.newpage()
grid.draw(gr)
```

## Comparisons

### 'gridtext'

['gridtext'](https://wilkelab.org/gridtext/) by Claus O. Wilke (used by
['ggtext'](https://wilkelab.org/ggtext/)) renders formatted text via a subset
of HTML/CSS. 'munch' takes a different approach: it uses markdown or 'flextable'
chunks as input and relies on 'systemfonts' for text measurement.

| | munch | gridtext |
|---|---|---|
| Input format | Markdown, flextable chunks | HTML / CSS subset |
| Superscript / subscript | Yes (`as_sup()`, `as_sub()`) | Yes (`<sup>`, `<sub>`) |
| Custom colors / highlight | Yes (via `colorize()`, `as_highlight()`) | Yes (via inline CSS) |
| Inline images | Yes | Yes |
| Text wrapping | Yes | Yes (`textbox_grob()`) |
| Text measurement | TBD | TBD |
| Integration with 'flextable' | Yes (shared chunk model) | No |
| Supported devices | 'ragg', 'svglite', 'ggiraph', cairo | Most R graphic devices |
| Compiled code | No (pure R) | Yes (C++ via 'Rcpp') |

### with 'marquee'

['marquee'](https://marquee.r-lib.org/) by Thomas Lin Pedersen offers more
markdown features (headings, lists, code blocks, custom spans). 'munch' focuses
first on integration with 'flextable' chunks and advanced
formatting not available in markdown.

- 'munch' works with 'ragg', 'svglite', 'ggiraph', `cairo_pdf()`, `png(type = "cairo")`, eventually `pdf()` with
few cautions.
- 'marquee' works on a wide range of R devices but not yet with 'svglite' or 'ggiraph'.
- If working with markdown, 'munch' expect only a single paragraph, 'marquee'
can handle many markdown blocks in one call.
